# Native gRPC merchant and operator workspace

Turn selected unary methods from a private protobuf service into the original
Stellar Forge seller's paid JSON routes. Capture the actual protobuf import
closure, review exact request and response types, retain a plan with complete
payment terms, and operate the merchant through the original SF30 and SF82
lifecycles.

The workspace provides source and plan revisions, typed request editing, channel
review, explicit upstream calls with retained outcomes, merchant preparation,
customer downloads and the original release control. The upstream target, local
protobuf files, certificate material and credential values stay on the merchant
side. Buyers select an advertised HTTP route and send its JSON request.

## Start from source

Use Node 22.16 or later. Install the optional native transport in this folder:

~~~sh
npm ci --prefix stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc \
  --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
~~~

The committed transport closure pins @grpc/grpc-js 1.13.4, @grpc/proto-loader 0.8.1
and protobufjs 7.6.6. The same resolved protobufjs module must serve the original
loader and this source compiler. Compilation verifies the actual loader's
64-bit, boolean and string-map behavior, including legitimate own keys named
__proto__, constructor and the empty string. Public JSON stays canonical; the
adapter applies only the measured native serializer's representation internally.

The original native payment SDK is optional. With no facilitator selected, the
seller runs in CHALLENGE_ONLY mode and never executes a paid application route.
The workspace's explicit **Run upstream request** action directly calls the
merchant's own upstream; its button makes that action distinct and retains an
operation ID.

Launch a new empty private workspace:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/workspace/server.mjs \
  --state /private/merchant/grpc-workspace --port 8453
~~~

Open the complete private URL printed by the server. Its capability remains in
the browser session. The HTTP listener binds to 127.0.0.1 and requires the
original capability on API requests. Keep the state directory outside the
source checkout and installed software directory.

## Open from installed Applications

In the original Runtime workspace, select the installed runtime with the gRPC
transport and add a **gRPC merchant authoring** application. Choose its private
workspace directory, listener port and, when needed, the original private
environment file. Review the saved selection, then Start and open the private
workspace URL shown by the managed application.

Applications opens this same operator workspace. Source capture, typed request
editing, explicit native calls, payment terms, merchant preparation and SF82
release control stay in their original screens and retained files. Start checks
the reviewed workspace identity, current source revision and selected native
launcher bytes before announcing a live authenticated session.

Use the original application's Stop action to drain its merchant and native
calls. Reopen uses the same private state and shows prior outcomes; it does not
repeat an earlier application RPC or silently restart a seller. A changed current
revision needs a fresh Start review. The complete field, startup, recovery and
installation instructions are in
[Managed gRPC Applications](../../distribution/runtime-workspace/GRPC_APPLICATIONS.md).

## Operate the included native example

The included example is a real gRPC server with three clearly labelled local
demonstration rows. It exposes Summary and a visible streaming Watch method.
Only Summary can become a paid unary route.

In one terminal, choose an example-only authorization value and start the server:

~~~sh
export GRPC_DEMO_AUTHORIZATION='local-example-only'
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/examples/server.mjs \
  --port 50051
~~~

Start the workspace from a second terminal with the same environment value.
Select **Load included example**, then **Capture and save source**. The example's
merchant terms contain nonpayable asset and recipient markers. Replace those
with the merchant's actual approved terms before using a real payment network.

The response includes the exact record identifier 18446744073709551615, a decimal
amount stored as a string, base64 evidence bytes and a signed 64-bit sequence.
Those values travel through the real protobuf serializer and original gRPC
transport. The example's rows are documentation data, not a claim about an
external account.

## Capture and revise the merchant

1. On **Source**, select the exact upstream host:port and TLS or plaintext
   transport. Supply environment variable names for metadata and optional TLS
   credentials. Set the merchant-host protobuf directory and one or more entry
   files, then capture. Imported local files and required standard descriptors
   are retained with their source identities.
2. On **Methods & terms**, choose a captured unary method. Streaming methods
   remain visible but cannot be selected for these request/response HTTP routes.
3. Edit the exact request JSON or the generated fields. Inclusion checkboxes
   distinguish absent fields from explicit false, zero and empty values. Nested
   messages, maps and repeated values use JSON. The complete request and response
   schemas remain available beside the editor.
4. Define its route ID, public POST path, service name, description and complete
   ordered payment options. Amounts are quoted atomic-unit strings. Preserve
   scheme, network, asset, recipient, timeout and extra data for every option.
   Apply the route to the draft, then save the revision.
5. **Review channel and terms** compiles the retained contract and waits for
   native channel readiness. It sends no application RPC and does not claim that
   an upstream business operation succeeded.
6. **Run upstream request** intentionally calls the selected approved method with
   the merchant's credentials. The workspace persists its input, operation ID
   and attempt before invoking the original transport.

Saving uses the exact revision opened in the editor as its comparison base.
Refreshing inventory never advances that base. If another window saved a newer
revision, Save returns a conflict. Open the new current revision to inspect and
compose the intended changes, or explicitly make an older saved revision current.
The server serializes writes under the original merchant state lease.

A captured contract is immutable for that revision. Editing the former .proto
files does not change a saved merchant. Capture again to propose a new revision.

## Native value contract

| Protobuf field | Public JSON |
| --- | --- |
| int64, uint64, sint64, fixed64, sfixed64 | Exact decimal string, within the field's signed or unsigned range |
| 32-bit integer | Exact JSON integer in the field's range |
| bytes | Canonical standard base64 string |
| enum | Declared name, or an int32 numeric value for an unknown enum value |
| boolean | JSON true or false |
| repeated field | JSON array |
| map | JSON object with exact protobuf key representation; 64-bit keys are decimal strings |
| message | Object using exact descriptor field names |
| absent field | Omitted; no defaults are fabricated |
| oneof | At most one member included |
| nonfinite float | Explicit string token Infinity, -Infinity or NaN |
| negative-zero float | Explicit string token -0 |

Standard protobuf types keep their message fields. Timestamp is not silently
converted to a JavaScript Date, and Any is not automatically unpacked. Unknown
message fields and unknown enum names are rejected with a correction location.

## Connection and limits

source.json records the target, transport mode, environment references and limits.
It contains no credential values. TLS uses the normal gRPC trust configuration,
with optional CA, client certificate and private-key PEM values read from named
environment variables. A client certificate and key must be supplied together.
An optional certificate server name belongs to this merchant configuration.

Metadata names are fixed by the merchant. Text values must be printable ASCII;
binary -bin metadata reads canonical base64. Metadata is never copied from buyer
headers. The caller does not accept buyer-selected targets, credentials, method
names or deadlines.

| Limit | Default | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native RPC timeout | 30,000 ms | 300,000 ms |
| Channel readiness timeout | 10,000 ms | 60,000 ms |
| Concurrent native calls | 64 | 1,024 |
| Protobuf request bytes | 1 MiB | 8 MiB |
| Protobuf response bytes | 1 MiB | 8 MiB |
| JSON request bytes | 2 MiB | 16 MiB |
| JSON response bytes | 2 MiB | 16 MiB |
| Complete captured proto-source JSON | 8 MiB | 8 MiB |
| Selected merchant routes | — | 64 |

The compiled original seller receives the same JSON request/response limits and
handler timeout. Its complete HTTP request lifetime includes another 120 seconds
for the original body, admission and payment work. An HTTP disconnect or original
handler cancellation cancels the native call. Capacity stays occupied until the
native callback finishes, and shutdown waits for those callbacks.

The original seller still applies its own route, schema and payment-envelope
limits. A valid large protobuf closure may need a smaller selected public method
set to fit the advertised buyer contract. The compiler reports that concrete
limit before publishing a prepared merchant.

## Retained operations and recovery

Every intentional workspace RPC has a unique operation ID. The input and attempt
are durable before the call. A completed output is published as a compact
create-only snapshot before the completion receipt. Reading an operation after
a lost response recovers that same retained output. Reusing an operation ID with
different input is rejected.

ATTEMPTED and OUTCOME_UNCONFIRMED are visible because a lost transport reply does
not identify the upstream business outcome. Read the original operation and
inspect the upstream's actual state; a new intentional request gets a new ID.
The workspace never automatically repeats an uncertain application operation.
This does not add an upstream idempotency mechanism or change that service's
own mutation semantics.

Preparing a merchant is source compilation. It retains an intent, writes an
unpublished folder, then atomically publishes the finished original output.
Resume reuses the same preparation ID. If the folder was already published
before interruption, the workspace verifies it and consumes the remaining
intent. It does not execute an application RPC.

The original state lease prevents two workspace processes from writing the same
private state concurrently. Close the existing process normally before reopening.
Run state from a prior ended process is displayed explicitly; startup does not
silently launch another seller.

## Prepare, run and hand over

Choose **Prepare merchant** on a saved current revision. The private result
contains twelve original product files plus prepared.json:

- Connection, captured protobuf source and merchant plan.
- Original compiled service and method bindings.
- Public request/response method schemas and OpenAPI.
- Original generated JavaScript client, declarations, OpenAPI, package metadata
  and client guide.

**Run merchant** checks the retained files and native channel, then starts the
original seller and its operations console. Open merchant documentation,
OpenAPI, operations and availability from **Running merchant**. **Drain and stop**
uses the original seller's lifecycle before closing the gRPC channel.

**Customer client archive** contains exactly seven public files: methods.json,
openapi.json and the five generated client files. It excludes source.json,
proto-source.json, merchant-plan.json, retained calls and private state. Individual
downloads are checked against their retained file identities.

The response type is advertised through the original Bazaar output-example
schema. The live seller's OpenAPI and its generated customer download project
that same schema; prepared and live documentation do not rely on separate schema
generation.

## Stage, activate and roll back through SF82

Stop the workspace's direct merchant before release control. Enter a release
name on a prepared folder and select **Stage in release control**. The adapter
captures the complete twelve-file package and original manifest into the
existing SF82 store. **Open release control** opens the original application.

Use its ordinary compare, activate, run, drain, stop and rollback controls. Each
release retains the exact proto closure, selected method schemas, complete
payment options, environment variable names, limits and original customer files.
The former prepared directory can be moved after staging. Starting or rolling
back the retained release uses its captured package and the host environment
snapshot passed through the original child manager.

The original manager owns child startup and shutdown. The gRPC adapter adds a
source family; it does not create another release store or payment engine.
Closing the workspace closes its owned release console and uses its original
shutdown path.

Command-line source preparation is available for operators who already maintain
their source and plan:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/cli.mjs capture \
  --directory /private/proto --entry analytics.proto \
  --out /private/captured-proto.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/cli.mjs inspect \
  --proto /private/captured-proto.json \
  --method /stellarforge.analytics.v1.Analytics/Summary

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/cli.mjs prepare \
  --source /private/source.json --proto /private/captured-proto.json \
  --plan /private/merchant-plan.json --out /private/prepared-v1

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/grpc/start.mjs \
  --directory /private/prepared-v1 --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
~~~

Add the original facilitator URL with --facilitator when selecting native
payments. The explicit --allow-local-facilitator flag applies only to a loopback
HTTP facilitator. Configure actual network and recipient terms before using a
real facilitator. No signer is stored by this merchant workspace.

## Installed product

The original distribution catalog adds grpc, grpc-contract, grpc-workspace and
grpc-example, plus the grpc optional runtime feature. Its dependencies come from
this exact package.json, and its source archive includes the original .proto
example and browser asset manifest. API exports include merchant, source, config,
proto, values, prepare, workspace and retained-release entry points.

A selected portable release exposes the commands through its original launcher:

~~~sh
node /installation/forge.mjs run grpc-workspace -- \
  --state /private/merchant/grpc-workspace --port 8453
node /installation/forge.mjs doctor --feature grpc
~~~

Use the maintained release's optional runtime installation procedure. In a
portable release directory, npm install --ignore-scripts --omit=dev installs its
declared optional closure. Configuration and data remain outside the release,
so software activation and rollback retain merchant work.

The source package has no test runner or hosted Actions entrypoint. The included
server and operator commands are usable product examples. Native operating
results identify their actual source/runtime selection separately.

### Working editor changes

Typed request fields and the exact JSON editor share the same request. Invalid visible input prevents a call or route application. A working request can be called without adding it to the saved merchant plan; Apply route retains it as the route example. Complete plan JSON is explicitly applied or discarded before Save, channel review or Prepare. Opening another method, route, revision or the included example asks before discarding current work. A later inventory refresh keeps the exact opened revision as the editor's save base.

# Stellar RPC merchant

Sell selected Stellar RPC reads through the existing native seller, buyer and
operations workspace. Each selected method becomes one priced `POST` route at
`/stellar/METHOD`. Buyers send that method's parameters as a JSON object; the
merchant supplies the fixed JSON-RPC method and correlation ID and preserves the
provider's successful response bytes.

The adapter includes the whole operator path: review public terms, prepare the
original merchant package, check the selected data network, start the seller,
prepare a buyer request, inspect delivery, and pause or resume selected products
with the original persistent availability controls.

For a retained browser workflow, open the [merchant workspace](workspace/README.md):

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/jsonrpc/cli.mjs workspace \
  --dir /absolute/private/rpc-workspace --create --plan /absolute/private/rpc-plan.json
```

The same installed command is `starforge jsonrpc workspace`. The workspace
keeps exact imported plans, immutable saved versions, product/price comparisons,
original prepared packages, explicit provider diagnoses and buyer reviews.
Choose the runtime mode in its launcher to start the same original merchant
and operations desk from the selected saved review, then drain and reopen the
retained workspace.

Use the same prepared package in the [native release lifecycle](../../sf82-seller-pilot/JSONRPC_RELEASES.md)
with `starforge releases stage --store PRIVATE_STORE --id RELEASE --jsonrpc-package PREPARED_PACKAGE`.
That path retains the complete original package, compares versions, selects and
rolls back releases, and opens this merchant's original operations controls from
the existing release console or merchant MCP client.

## 1. Choose the product and payment terms

Run these commands from the source checkout with its existing Node and native
seller dependencies installed:

```sh
RPC=stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/jsonrpc/cli.mjs
install -d -m 700 /srv/stellar-rpc
node "$RPC" template > /srv/stellar-rpc/plan.json
```

The adjacent [example-plan.json](example-plan.json) is a three-product starting
point. Replace the origin, recipient, asset contract and every price before
inspection. Prices are positive integer **strings in the selected asset's atomic
units**. Use the merchant's actual payment terms; the example has deliberately
unfinished values.

`dataNetwork` selects `stellar:testnet` or `stellar:pubnet`. `payment.network`
identifies the network on which the buyer pays. Review both explicitly; a
testnet-priced demonstration can read a different declared data network. The
merchant compares the provider's `getNetwork` passphrase with `dataNetwork`
before opening its listeners.

Choose only the methods and per-request prices the merchant intends to sell:

| Method | Buyer body | Returned data and request limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getTransaction` | `hash`; optional `xdrFormat:"base64"` | One lowercase 64-character transaction hash. `SUCCESS`, `FAILED` and `NOT_FOUND` are valid lookup outcomes. |
| `getTransactions` | `startLedger` or `pagination.cursor`; optional `pagination.limit` | Transaction history; maximum 200 records per page, default 50 or the configured lower maximum. |
| `getEvents` | Ledger window or cursor, optional filters and limit | Contract/system events; default 100 per page, configured maximum 500 by default and at most 10,000. |
| `getLedgerEntries` | `keys`; optional `xdrFormat:"base64"` | Current ledger state; 1–200 distinct canonical base64 LedgerKey values, subject to the configured maximum. |
| `getLedgers` | `startLedger` or `pagination.cursor`; optional `pagination.limit` | Ledger history; maximum 200 records per page, default 50 or the configured lower maximum. |
| `getFeeStats` | `{}` | Current inclusion-fee statistics. |
| `getHealth` | `{}` | Node health and available ledger window. |
| `getLatestLedger` | `{}` | Latest known ledger identity and sequence. |
| `getNetwork` | `{}` | Selected network passphrase and protocol version. |
| `getVersionInfo` | `{}` | RPC server version information. |

Requests use named parameter objects. This product fixes XDR-bearing responses
to base64 so the buyer can decode them with its existing Stellar SDK. The event
filter profile supports `system`/`contract`, up to five filters and five contract
IDs across the request, and up to five topic alternatives with one to four
base64 ScVal or `*` segments. The profile's OpenAPI and prepayment admission
describe the exact selected subset of the Stellar methods.

For a first history page, select an actual `startLedger` within the provider's
current retained window. `getEvents.endLedger` is exclusive. For subsequent
pages, use the returned `pagination.cursor` and omit the ledger bounds. Each
page is a separately priced request. The zero hash and ledger 1 in generated
schema examples illustrate input shape; use actual observed identifiers when
preparing a purchase.

```sh
node "$RPC" inspect --plan /srv/stellar-rpc/plan.json
node "$RPC" prepare --plan /srv/stellar-rpc/plan.json \
  --out /srv/stellar-rpc/prepared-v1
```

`inspect` and `prepare` operate offline. Preparation creates a new private
directory containing `plan.json`, `openapi.json`, `selections.json`,
`route-bindings.json`, `seller-offers.json`, a trusted `handlers.mjs`, the
original SF61 `compiled/` output, and an executable-command guide in `RUN.md`.
Its parent directory must already be private, and the destination must be new.
Retain that package and its complete immutable source checkout for the release.

## 2. Supply the original provider connection

`endpointEnv` names the environment variable containing the complete provider
RPC URL. Supply its value through the service's existing private environment or
secret manager. A URL with an API key in its path stays in the launch-time
connection; the plan contains only the variable name.

The endpoint is a canonical public HTTPS URL with a fixed path, separate from
the merchant's origin. Query strings, fragments, user-info and buyer-selected
destinations are outside this connection contract. Normal launch reuses the
original upstream DNS, TLS, redirect, timeout, response-size and concurrency
handling. Local development can explicitly select
`--allow-loopback-upstream` for a local provider.

Providers using credential headers can add the original declaration:

```json
"headerEnv": { "Authorization": "STELLAR_RPC_AUTHORIZATION" }
```

The named variable holds the complete header value. The original `oauth2`
declaration is also supported; use the existing
[upstream authentication guide](../UPSTREAM.md) and the same provider's actual
client-credentials configuration. OAuth owns its authorization header. Caller
payment headers and cookies are not forwarded to the provider.

```sh
node "$RPC" diagnose --plan /srv/stellar-rpc/prepared-v1/plan.json
```

Diagnosis makes one `getNetwork` and one `getHealth` provider read and prints
network, protocol and retention metadata. These use the provider account's
normal request allowance. Repeated diagnosis commands are new processes and
make new reads. Use the reported `oldestLedger`/`latestLedger` to prepare a
current history request.

The response contract follows the current
[Stellar RPC API](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods).
In particular, `getTransaction` includes a numeric `latestLedger` and the queried
`txHash`; current health includes the ledger window. Some provider documentation
still illustrates earlier response formats. Confirm that the selected endpoint
serves the current API when qualifying a deployment. The original response
contract validates the actual returned envelope before accepting a successful
product result.

## 3. Run the merchant and its private desk

Use the same prepared plan, a stable merchant HTTPS origin, and separate private
state directories. Put the public merchant hostname behind the deployment's
existing HTTPS ingress while preserving `/stellar/*` and original discovery
paths. The seller and operations listeners bind locally.

```sh
node "$RPC" serve --plan /srv/stellar-rpc/prepared-v1/plan.json \
  --facilitator https://YOUR_ACTUAL_FACILITATOR \
  --port 8423 --operations-port 8424 \
  --availability-dir /srv/stellar-rpc/availability \
  --history-dir /srv/stellar-rpc/history --history-days 90 \
  --state /srv/stellar-rpc/delivery
```

`--state` attaches the original native delivery outbox and requires the selected
facilitator. Availability uses the existing Linux `flock` single-writer policy.
The operations desk retains the original seller's outcomes and in-flight work.
Capacity defaults to 64 admitted seller requests; each selected RPC binding
defaults to eight provider requests. `--max-in-flight` and
`--drain-grace-ms` configure the original seller lifecycle.

For a challenge preview, replace the facilitator and delivery-state options
with `--challenge-only`. Both modes verify the data network with one provider
read at startup. Challenge mode displays the original payment offers; the paid
delivery path uses the native facilitator mode above.

Startup reports the original discovery and operations URLs, including the
availability desk and its private control URL. Keep the operations listener
private. Open the merchant's `/_seller/docs` explorer for public requests and
offers. Changing an environment variable does not change a running connection:
drain and restart the merchant with the new provider value, the same plan and
the same state directories.

## 4. Prepare and run the original buyer workflow

Save the actual **params object** to a private request file. For a transaction
read it contains `{"hash":"ACTUAL_64_CHARACTER_LOWERCASE_TRANSACTION_HASH"}`.
For a metadata product it contains `{}`. The merchant supplies `jsonrpc`,
`method` and `id` on the provider request.

```sh
node "$RPC" buyer --package /srv/stellar-rpc/prepared-v1 \
  --method getTransaction --body-file /srv/stellar-rpc/request.json \
  --intent-id YOUR_STABLE_PURCHASE_ID \
  --out /srv/stellar-rpc/buyer-review.json
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/cli.mjs \
  --review --config /srv/stellar-rpc/buyer-review.json
```

The buyer command applies the same selected input contract and prepares the
existing SF88 review configuration. Continue with that buyer's original native
workspace, signer selection, challenge review and purchase action. Preserve the
original intent and operation when reopening a delivery or reconciling a lost
response. Select a new intent for a deliberately new purchase or next page.

Successful delivery preserves the complete provider JSON-RPC envelope, including
the fixed correlation ID `sf30:METHOD`. Read the method result under `result`.
The original bytes retain large integer literals and extra result fields. A
transaction's `FAILED` or `NOT_FOUND` status describes chain data; merchant
payment and settlement status comes from the original buyer operation.

## 5. Operate, pause and recover

Use the returned private `availabilityControl` URL in
`SELLER_AVAILABILITY_URL`, then inspect the current revision and route IDs:

```sh
S=stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk
node "$S/availability/cli.mjs" status --url http://127.0.0.1:8424
node "$S/availability/cli.mjs" pause --url-env SELLER_AVAILABILITY_URL \
  --revision REVIEWED_REVISION --route REVIEWED_ROUTE_ID \
  --reason 'Provider maintenance'
```

Use `resume` with the next reviewed revision after restoring service. The same
desk supports selecting several products and reviewing recent changes. Pausing
rejects new requests before payment while admitted requests drain; sibling
products remain available. Saved pauses survive the original service's restart.
A stale revision returns a conflict with current state for deliberate review.
The [availability guide](../availability/README.md) describes the existing API,
CLI, retired route IDs and persistent policy.

| Observed outcome | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid parameters (`422`) | Correct the selected params using the published schema and actual retained ledger window. |
| Network preflight fails | Confirm the endpoint, current provider API, access and `dataNetwork`; diagnose that same connection before restart. |
| Provider/RPC/result contract fails or times out (`502`/`504`) | Inspect the original operator outcome and provider status; retain the buyer's current operation while reconciling payment state. |
| Provider admission or capacity (`429`/`503`) | Inspect the existing upstream availability counters and retry delay, then deliberately select the next request. |
| Paused or draining product (`503`) | Read the existing private availability/lifecycle view and resume the intended route when service is restored. |
| Lost response or interrupted buyer | Reopen the original buyer operation and delivery record before starting another purchase. |

The optional `upstreamAvailability` plan section reuses the existing
[upstream health policy](../UPSTREAM_AVAILABILITY.md). It governs provider
admission separately from the operator's durable route pause. `SIGINT` and
`SIGTERM` use the original merchant close path: finish seller payment and
handler work, finish the operations observer, then release the upstream and
OAuth resources.

## Embedding and source composition

Import `startStellarRpcMerchant` from `merchant.mjs` for the combined listener
lifecycle. It accepts the plan, environment, original native factory and the
same availability/history/delivery options and returns the original seller
session plus `operations`, `application` and a combined `close()`.

Trusted existing hosts can use `createStellarRpcApplication` from
`application.mjs`. Await `verifyNetwork()` before admitting work, attach its
`config` and `handlers` to the original seller, and call `close()` after that
seller drains. `diagnose()` adds the original health read; `snapshot()` reports
current method/network/provider counters. The generated trusted handler entry
performs the network check before exporting its handlers and exports cleanup.

Keep the full SF30 source, original SF61 compiler, SF88 buyer and their existing
dependency closure together. `stellar.mjs` imports the already-released request
and admission functions from
`../../partners/getblock-stellar/product.mjs`; that module and its original
SF61 imports are required even when the selected provider is different.

The method contracts were checked against the official
[transaction](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getTransaction),
[transaction history](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getTransactions),
[events](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getEvents),
[ledger entries](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getLedgerEntries),
[ledgers](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getLedgers),
[health](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getHealth)
and [network](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getNetwork)
references. The source intentionally uses one existing payment engine,
provider transport, buyer review and operating lifecycle throughout.
